content:
The [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Encode Unicode text as Base64 directly in your browser. Enter your text and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like. It is one of the [Web & Developer tools](/tools?category=Web%20%26%20Developer) on CalcHub — the others work the same way.

Encode Unicode text as Base64 directly in your browser. This free online base64 encoder gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Base64 Encoder

Start by typing or pasting your text. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste your text.
2. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
3. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

UTF-8 bytes are grouped into 6-bit chunks and represented by the Base64 alphabet.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Hello becomes SGVsbG8=. Try the same figures in the [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Text: Hello, CalcHub! Café déjà vu), the [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) returns Base64: SGVsbG8sIENhbGNIdWIhIENhZsOpIGTDqWrDoCB2dQ==. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [URL Encoder](/url-encoder) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this base64 encoder free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Base64 Encoder use?

UTF-8 bytes are grouped into 6-bit chunks and represented by the Base64 alphabet. You can see it in action in the [Base64 Encoder](/base64-encoder) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Base64 Encoder?

Just Text. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
